```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggraph)
library(tidygraph)
library(igraph)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
library(kableExtra)

# Custom transparent theme for slides
theme_slides <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_graph() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    legend.text = element_text(color = "#2c3e50", size = 11, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = base_size * 1.2, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, color = "#2c3e50"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_size * 1.0, hjust = 0.5, color = "#7f8c8d"),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  dev = "png",
  dev.args = list(bg = "transparent")
)

pos_col <- "forestgreen"
neg_col <- "firebrick"

# Circle layout: nodes placed clockwise starting at 12 o'clock
circ_lay <- function(names, start = pi/2) {
  n <- length(names)
  ang <- start - (0:(n - 1)) * (2 * pi / n)
  m <- cbind(x = cos(ang), y = sin(ang))
  rownames(m) <- names
  m
}

# Node fill colors by membership map; unmapped nodes get the default
fill_vec <- function(names, map, default = "#ecf0f1") {
  out <- rep(default, length(names)); names(out) <- names
  hit <- intersect(names, names(map)); out[hit] <- map[hit]
  out
}

# Standard signed-edge layer + scales for an undirected signed graph
edge_layer <- function(width = 2.2) {
  geom_edge_link(aes(color = sign, linetype = sign), width = width,
                 end_cap = circle(10, "mm"), start_cap = circle(10, "mm"))
}
edge_scales <- function() {
  list(
    scale_edge_color_manual(values = c("+" = pos_col, "-" = neg_col, "±" = "#7d3c98")),
    scale_edge_linetype_manual(values = c("+" = "solid", "-" = "33", "±" = "13"))
  )
}

# P-O-Q triad panel (edge order P-O, O-Q, P-Q); directed sentiments
triad_panel <- function(signs, ttl = NULL, node_size = 14, lab = 5) {
  e <- data.frame(from = c("P", "O", "P"), to = c("O", "Q", "Q"), sign = signs)
  g <- graph_from_data_frame(e, directed = TRUE)
  ggraph(g, layout = circ_lay(c("P", "O", "Q"))) +
    geom_edge_link(aes(color = sign, linetype = sign),
                   arrow = arrow(length = unit(3.5, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                   width = 1.8, end_cap = circle(9, "mm"), start_cap = circle(9, "mm")) +
    geom_node_point(size = node_size, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.4) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = lab, color = "#2c3e50") +
    edge_scales() +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25), ylim = c(-0.95, 1.3), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                           plot.title = element_text(size = 9)) +
    ggtitle(ttl)
}

# kable helper for signed adjacency matrices; colors +1 green, -1 red
signed_kbl <- function(m, font = 20, color_cells = TRUE) {
  mm <- m
  if (color_cells) {
    mm[] <- vapply(m, function(v) {
      dplyr::case_when(
        v == "1"  ~ cell_spec(v, background = "#ABEBC6"),
        v == "-1" ~ cell_spec(v, background = "#F5B7B1"),
        TRUE ~ v
      )
    }, "")
    dim(mm) <- dim(m); dimnames(mm) <- dimnames(m)
  }
  knitr::kable(mm, format = "html", escape = FALSE) |>
    kable_styling(font_size = font, full_width = FALSE, position = "center")
}

# Complete signed graph between/within named groups
comp_pairs <- function(g1, g2, sign) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(g1, function(i) do.call(rbind, lapply(g2, function(j)
    data.frame(from = i, to = j, sign = sign)))))
}
```

# Part 1: Dyadic Balance Theory

---

## Balance Theory and Signed Graphs
### The Local and Global Dynamics of Valenced Networks

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Relationships are not just present or absent; they carry emotional **valence**.
- **Balance Theory** is the foundational framework linking:
  - Local, psychological micro-motives.
  - Global, macro-structural network patterns (like polarization).
- Today we will cover: Dyadic Balance, Signed Graphs, Triadic Balance, Structural Balance, and Clusterability.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 5
#| fig.height: 5
triad_panel(c("+", "+", "-"), node_size = 20, lab = 6)
```
:::
:::

---

## Dyadic Balance: From Similarities to Interactions

::: {.incremental}
- Ideas of dyadic balance were first described in a famous paper written by **Fritz Heider** in 1946.
- Ties differ based on whether they are based on:
  - **Similarities**.
  - **Interactions**.
- The basic principle is that people seek balance between similarities and interactions.
  - People tend to interact with people who are similar to them.
- If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are two people, $S$ is a tie based on similarity and $R$ is a tie based on interaction:

$$\alpha S \beta \rightarrow \alpha R \beta$$
:::

---

## Dyadic Balance: Reading the Principle

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
::: {.incremental}
- $\alpha S \beta \rightarrow \alpha R \beta$ reads: **"A tie of type $S$ between $\alpha$ and $\beta$ leads to a tie of type $R$ between $\alpha$ and $\beta$."**
- This applies to **every combination** of similarities and interactions.
- Examples:
  - People tend to **like** the people they **spend time with**.
  - People tend to **help** people who **belong to the same groups** as them.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.6
#| fig.height: 3.5
# Similarity tie feeding an interaction tie (alpha S beta -> alpha R beta)
e <- data.frame(from = c("α", "β"), to = c("β", "α"), type = c("S", "R"))
g <- graph_from_data_frame(e, directed = TRUE)
lay <- circ_lay(c("α", "β"))
S_idx <- function(l) { ed <- get_edges()(l); ed[ed$type == "S", ] }
R_idx <- function(l) { ed <- get_edges()(l); ed[ed$type == "R", ] }
ggraph(g, layout = lay) +
  geom_edge_arc(data = S_idx, aes(color = type), width = 2.4, strength = -0.35,
                end_cap = circle(11, "mm"), start_cap = circle(11, "mm")) +
  geom_edge_arc(data = R_idx, aes(color = type), width = 2.4, strength = -0.35,
                end_cap = circle(11, "mm"), start_cap = circle(11, "mm")) +
  geom_edge_arc(data = R_idx, width = 2.4, strength = -0.35, show.legend = FALSE,
                color = pos_col,
                arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                end_cap = circle(11, "mm"), start_cap = circle(11, "mm")) +
  geom_node_point(size = 22, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.8) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 8, color = "#2c3e50") +
  scale_edge_color_manual(values = c("S" = "#2980b9", "R" = pos_col),
                          labels = c("S = similarity tie", "R = interaction tie")) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.3, 1.3), ylim = c(-1.0, 1.0), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank())
```
:::
:::

---

## What Counts as Similarities and Interactions?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **Similarities**
  - Propinquity (same place).
  - Homophily (same social category).
  - Co-memberships (same social groups).
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **Interactions**
  - Communicating with.
  - Liking.
  - Helping.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.incremental}
- Reference: Borgatti, S. P., Mehra, A., Brass, D. J., & Labianca, G. (2009). Network analysis in the social sciences. *Science*, 323(5916), 892–895.
:::

---

## Worked Example: Spending Time and Liking

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **Balanced**: Simbi and Keryl spend time together **and** like each other.
  - Similarity and interaction point the same way.
- **Unbalanced**: Simbi and Keryl spend time together, but the liking is one-sided.
  - A similarity paired with a missing or hostile interaction creates tension.
- Balance theory predicts the tension gets resolved: the liking becomes mutual, or the time spent together dries up.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.6
#| fig.height: 4.4
# Two dyads: mutual liking (balanced) vs one-sided liking (unbalanced)
dyad_panel <- function(mutual, ttl) {
  e <- data.frame(from = c("Simbi", "Keryl"), to = c("Keryl", "Simbi"))
  g <- graph_from_data_frame(e[if (mutual) c(1, 2) else 1, ], directed = TRUE)
  lay <- circ_lay(c("Simbi", "Keryl"))
  like_S2K <- function(l) { ed <- get_edges()(l)
    ed[ed$from == match("Simbi", V(g)$name) & ed$to == match("Keryl", V(g)$name), ] }
  like_K2S <- function(l) { ed <- get_edges()(l)
    ed[ed$from == match("Keryl", V(g)$name), ] }
  p <- ggraph(g, layout = lay) +
    geom_edge_arc(data = like_S2K, width = 2, strength = 0.35, color = pos_col,
                  arrow = arrow(length = unit(3.5, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                  end_cap = circle(11, "mm"), start_cap = circle(11, "mm"))
  if (mutual) {
    p <- p + geom_edge_arc(data = like_K2S, width = 2, strength = 0.35, color = pos_col,
                  arrow = arrow(length = unit(3.5, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                  end_cap = circle(11, "mm"), start_cap = circle(11, "mm"))
  }
  p +
    geom_edge_arc(width = 2.4, strength = 0, color = "#2980b9",
                  end_cap = circle(12, "mm"), start_cap = circle(12, "mm")) +
    geom_node_point(size = 20, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.8) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 5.5, color = "#2c3e50") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-0.8, 0.8), ylim = c(-1.05, 1.5), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                           plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold")) +
    ggtitle(ttl)
}
dyad_panel(TRUE, "Balanced") + dyad_panel(FALSE, "Unbalanced")
```

::: {.incremental}
- Solid green: liking (directed). Blue: spend time with (symmetric).
:::
:::
:::

---

## Worked Example: Same Groups and Helping

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **Balanced**: Simbi and Keryl belong to the same groups **and** help each other.
- **Unbalanced**: They share group memberships, but the helping only flows one way.
- Same logic, different content: any symmetric similarity tie wants to be matched by reciprocal interaction ties.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.6
#| fig.height: 4.4
# Same structure: shared group (symmetric) + help (directed)
help_panel <- function(mutual, ttl) {
  e <- data.frame(from = c("Simbi", "Keryl"), to = c("Keryl", "Simbi"))
  g <- graph_from_data_frame(e[if (mutual) c(1, 2) else 1, ], directed = TRUE)
  lay <- circ_lay(c("Simbi", "Keryl"))
  help_S2K <- function(l) { ed <- get_edges()(l)
    ed[ed$from == match("Simbi", V(g)$name) & ed$to == match("Keryl", V(g)$name), ] }
  help_K2S <- function(l) { ed <- get_edges()(l)
    ed[ed$from == match("Keryl", V(g)$name), ] }
  p <- ggraph(g, layout = lay) +
    geom_edge_arc(data = help_S2K, width = 2, strength = 0.35, color = pos_col,
                  arrow = arrow(length = unit(3.5, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                  end_cap = circle(11, "mm"), start_cap = circle(11, "mm"))
  if (mutual) {
    p <- p + geom_edge_arc(data = help_K2S, width = 2, strength = 0.35, color = pos_col,
                  arrow = arrow(length = unit(3.5, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                  end_cap = circle(11, "mm"), start_cap = circle(11, "mm"))
  }
  p +
    geom_edge_arc(width = 2.4, strength = 0, color = "#2980b9",
                  end_cap = circle(12, "mm"), start_cap = circle(12, "mm")) +
    geom_node_point(size = 20, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.8) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 5.5, color = "#2c3e50") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-0.8, 0.8), ylim = c(-1.05, 1.5), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                           plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold")) +
    ggtitle(ttl)
}
help_panel(TRUE, "Balanced") + help_panel(FALSE, "Unbalanced")
```

::: {.incremental}
- Solid green: help (directed). Blue: same group (symmetric).
:::
:::
:::

---

## The Cycle Runs Both Ways: From Interactions to Similarities

::: {.incremental}
- After the first cycle of similarities leading to interactions, **interactions can lead to further similarities**: $\alpha R \beta \rightarrow \alpha S \beta$.
- People tend to **think like** (share the opinions and attitudes of) the people they interact with.
- People tend to adopt the same **tastes and fashions** as the people in the same organizations as them.
- People tend to **spend time with** the people they like.
- Similarities and interactions feed each other in a continuing loop.
:::

---

# Part 2: Signed Graphs

---

## Signed Graphs

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Signed graphs are a special kind of graph featuring:
  - One set of vertices $V$.
  - **Two disjoint sets of edges**:
    - Positive links ($E^+$).
    - Negative links ($E^-$).
- The graph is written $G = \{V, E^+, E^-\}$.
- Two sets are **disjoint** when they don't share any members (their intersection is the empty set $\emptyset$).
- Signed graphs can be either **directed or undirected**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-sg5
#| fig.width: 4.4
#| fig.height: 4.4
# Five-node undirected signed graph
sg5_e <- data.frame(
  from = c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C", "D"),
  to   = c("C", "D", "C", "E", "D", "E", "E"),
  sign = c("-", "+", "+", "+", "-", "+", "-")
)
sg5 <- graph_from_data_frame(sg5_e, directed = FALSE)
ggraph(sg5, layout = circ_lay(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"))) +
  edge_layer() + edge_scales() +
  geom_node_point(size = 17, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.7) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 6, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ggtitle("Undirected signed graph")
```
:::
:::


# Part 3: Triadic Balance Theory

---

## Balance Theory

::: {.incremental}
- Balance theory is a **social psychological theory** designed to explain expected triadic configurations in sentiment networks.
- Sentiment networks are built from **valenced ties** (e.g., positive or negative).
- There are **four building blocks** in balance theory.
:::

---

## Building Block 1: A Person (P)

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {.incremental}
- The **person (P)**.
- We "look" at the triad from this person's point of view.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 3.4
#| fig.height: 3.6
g <- make_empty_graph(n = 0) + vertices("P")
ggraph(g, layout = cbind(x = 0, y = 0)) +
  geom_node_point(size = 26, fill = "#d4edda", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.8) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 8, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::
:::

---

## Building Block 2: An Object (O)

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {.incremental}
- An **object (O)** towards which the focal person has some kind of sentiment.
- The sentiment can be positive or negative.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 3.6
#| fig.height: 3.6
e <- data.frame(from = "P", to = "O")
g <- graph_from_data_frame(e, directed = TRUE)
ggraph(g, layout = circ_lay(c("P", "O"))) +
  geom_edge_link(arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                 width = 2, color = "#7f8c8d",
                 end_cap = circle(12, "mm"), start_cap = circle(12, "mm")) +
  geom_node_point(size = 24, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.8) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 8, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-0.85, 0.85), ylim = c(-1.05, 1.05), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::
:::

---

## Building Block 3: A Third Party (Q)

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {.incremental}
- A **third party (Q)** towards which both the person and the other also have some kind of sentiment.
- Q does not have to be a real person! It could be **any object**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 3.6
#| fig.height: 3.8
e <- data.frame(from = c("P", "O"), to = c("O", "Q"))
g <- graph_from_data_frame(e, directed = TRUE)
ggraph(g, layout = circ_lay(c("P", "O", "Q"))) +
  geom_edge_link(arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                 width = 2, color = "#7f8c8d",
                 end_cap = circle(11, "mm"), start_cap = circle(11, "mm")) +
  geom_node_point(size = 22, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.8) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 7, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.2, 1.2), ylim = c(-1.0, 1.3), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::
:::

---

## Building Block 4: Directed Signed Edges

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- A set of **directed signed edges** indicating positive (solid green) or negative (dashed red) sentiments:
  - From P to O.
  - From P to Q.
  - From O to Q.
- This configuration reads: Person (P) likes Other (O); Other (O) likes the third party (Q); but Person (P) dislikes the third party.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.2
triad_panel(c("+", "+", "-"), node_size = 18, lab = 6)
```
:::
:::

---

## The Triad in Everyday Terms

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.0
triad_panel(c("+", "+", "-"), node_size = 18, lab = 6)
```

::: {.incremental}
- **Sounds dicey!**
- You (P) have a friend (O) who likes another classmate (Q) whom you dislike.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.0
triad_panel(c("+", "+", "+"), node_size = 18, lab = 6)
```

::: {.incremental}
- **Everything's fine!**
- You (P) have a friend (O) who likes another classmate (Q) whom you also like.
:::
:::
:::

---

## The Triad in Everyday Terms (continued)

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.0
triad_panel(c("-", "+", "-"), node_size = 18, lab = 6)
```

::: {.incremental}
- **Seems fine?**
- You (P) have an enemy (O) who likes another classmate (Q) whom you also dislike.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.0
triad_panel(c("+", "-", "+"), node_size = 18, lab = 6)
```

::: {.incremental}
- **Trouble in paradise!**
- You (P) love Marvel movies (Q), but your long-time partner O (whom you like, duh!) hates them.
:::
:::
:::

---

## The Eight Configurations

::: {.incremental}
- There are eight (8) configurations, featuring one-way directed links from:
  - Person (P) to Other (O).
  - Person (P) to Third Party (Q).
  - Other (O) to Third Party (Q).
- Four of them are **balanced**; four are **unbalanced**.
:::

---

## Balanced Configurations

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 6
#| fig.height: 5
triad_panel(c("+", "+", "+"), "(+, +, +)") +
  triad_panel(c("-", "-", "+"), "(−, −, +)") +
  triad_panel(c("-", "+", "-"), "(−, +, −)") +
  triad_panel(c("+", "-", "-"), "(+, −, −)") +
  plot_layout(nrow = 2)
```
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- In each balanced configuration, the sentiments cohere.
- **"A friend of a friend is a friend."**
- **"An enemy of an enemy is a friend."**
- **"A friend of an enemy is an enemy."**
- **"An enemy of a friend is an enemy."**
:::
:::
:::

---

## Unbalanced Configurations

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 6
#| fig.height: 5
triad_panel(c("+", "+", "-"), "(+, +, −)") +
  triad_panel(c("+", "-", "+"), "(+, −, +)") +
  triad_panel(c("-", "+", "+"), "(−, +, +)") +
  triad_panel(c("-", "-", "-"), "(−, −, −)") +
  plot_layout(nrow = 2)
```
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- In each unbalanced configuration, the sentiments collide.
- **"A friend of my friend is my enemy."**
- **"An enemy of a friend is a friend."**
- **"A friend of an enemy is a friend."**
- **"An enemy of my enemy is also my enemy."**
:::
:::
:::

---

## Tension and Change

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- The basic idea is that **unbalanced configurations will tend to transition to balanced configurations**.
- Unbalanced configurations produce **tension in P**, leading them to change their sentiments toward O or Q to generate balance.
- Balanced configurations are stable **equilibrium states**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.4
#| fig.height: 4.4
# Unbalanced (+, +, -) transitions to balanced (+, +, +)
g1 <- graph_from_data_frame(data.frame(from = c("P", "O", "P"), to = c("O", "Q", "Q"),
                                       sign = c("+", "+", "-")), directed = TRUE)
g2 <- graph_from_data_frame(data.frame(from = c("P", "O", "P"), to = c("O", "Q", "Q"),
                                       sign = c("+", "+", "+")), directed = TRUE)
lay3 <- circ_lay(c("P", "O", "Q"))
tp <- function(g, ttl) {
  ggraph(g, layout = lay3) +
    geom_edge_link(aes(color = sign, linetype = sign),
                   arrow = arrow(length = unit(3.5, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                   width = 1.8, end_cap = circle(9, "mm"), start_cap = circle(9, "mm")) +
    geom_node_point(size = 15, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.5) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 5.5, color = "#2c3e50") +
    edge_scales() +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25), ylim = c(-0.95, 1.3), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                           plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold")) +
    ggtitle(ttl)
}
tp(g1, "Unbalanced") + tp(g2, "Balanced")
```
:::
:::

---

## The Mathematics of Balance Theory

::: {.incremental}
- Remember the rules of **sign multiplication** from basic algebra?

$$+1 \times +1 = +1 \qquad +1 \times -1 = -1 \qquad -1 \times -1 = +1$$
:::

::: {.incremental}
- They apply to balance theory!
:::

---

## Unbalanced Triads Have a Negative Product

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 6
#| fig.height: 5
triad_panel(c("+", "+", "-"), "(+, +, −)") +
  triad_panel(c("+", "-", "+"), "(+, −, +)") +
  triad_panel(c("-", "+", "+"), "(−, +, +)") +
  triad_panel(c("-", "-", "-"), "(−, −, −)") +
  plot_layout(nrow = 2)
```
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- If you multiply the signs of the edges of each **unbalanced** triad, you get a **negative** number. Try it!
- $(+1_{PO}) \times (+1_{OQ}) \times (-1_{PQ}) = -1_{POQ}$
- $(+1_{PO}) \times (-1_{OQ}) \times (+1_{PQ}) = -1_{POQ}$
- $(-1_{PO}) \times (+1_{OQ}) \times (+1_{PQ}) = -1_{POQ}$
- $(-1_{PO}) \times (-1_{OQ}) \times (-1_{PQ}) = -1_{POQ}$
:::
:::
:::

---

## Balanced Triads Have a Positive Product

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 6
#| fig.height: 5
triad_panel(c("-", "+", "-"), "(−, +, −)") +
  triad_panel(c("+", "-", "-"), "(+, −, −)") +
  triad_panel(c("-", "-", "+"), "(−, −, +)") +
  triad_panel(c("+", "+", "+"), "(+, +, +)") +
  plot_layout(nrow = 2)
```
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Conversely, if you multiply the signs of the edges of each **balanced** triad, you get a **positive** number.
- $(-1_{PO}) \times (+1_{OQ}) \times (-1_{PQ}) = +1_{POQ}$
- $(+1_{PO}) \times (-1_{OQ}) \times (-1_{PQ}) = +1_{POQ}$
- $(-1_{PO}) \times (-1_{OQ}) \times (+1_{PQ}) = +1_{POQ}$
- $(+1_{PO}) \times (+1_{OQ}) \times (+1_{PQ}) = +1_{POQ}$
:::
:::
:::

---

## A Link Between Mathematics and the Logic of Social Relations

::: {.incremental}
- **"A friend of a friend is a friend"**: $+1_{PO} \times +1_{OQ} \times +1_{PQ} = +1_{POQ}$
- **"An enemy of an enemy is a friend"**: $-1_{PO} \times -1_{OQ} \times +1_{PQ} = +1_{POQ}$
- **"A friend of an enemy is an enemy"**: $-1_{PO} \times +1_{OQ} \times -1_{PQ} = +1_{POQ}$
- **"An enemy of a friend is an enemy"**: $+1_{PO} \times -1_{OQ} \times -1_{PQ} = +1_{POQ}$
- Every folk rule for balanced sentiment is a sign product equal to $+1$.
:::

---

## Cross-Pressure

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Because we have multiple social relations, we are sometimes **caught between worlds**.
- This is called **cross-pressure**.
- Example: having two friends with **different attitudes towards the same object**.
- Balance theory predicts that P will have an **ambivalent** attitude toward the object.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.4
#| fig.height: 4.4
# P likes both friends; Friend 1 likes Taylor, Friend 2 dislikes Taylor;
# P's tie to Taylor is ambivalent (±)
xp_e <- data.frame(
  from = c("P", "P", "Friend 1", "Friend 2", "P"),
  to   = c("Friend 1", "Friend 2", "Taylor", "Taylor", "Taylor"),
  sign = c("+", "+", "+", "-", "±")
)
xp <- graph_from_data_frame(xp_e, directed = TRUE)
xp_lay <- rbind(c(0, 1.05), c(-0.95, -0.35), c(0.95, -0.35), c(0, -1.0))
rownames(xp_lay) <- c("P", "Friend 1", "Friend 2", "Taylor")
xp_plot <- function() {
  ggraph(xp, layout = xp_lay) +
    geom_edge_link(aes(color = sign, linetype = sign),
                   arrow = arrow(length = unit(3.5, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                   width = 1.8, end_cap = circle(10, "mm"), start_cap = circle(10, "mm")) +
    geom_node_point(size = 18, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.6) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 5, color = "#2c3e50") +
    edge_scales() +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25), ylim = c(-1.4, 1.45), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
}
xp_plot()
```
:::
:::

---

## Resolving Cross-Pressure

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- To achieve balance and remove the ambivalence, P can:
  - **Change** their own attitude toward Friend 1 or Friend 2.
  - **Convince** either Friend 1 or Friend 2 to change their attitude toward the object.
- The same tension-and-resolution logic that works triad by triad also works for whole networks. That is where we go next.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.2
xp_plot()
```
:::
:::

---

# Part 4: Structural Balance

---

## From Triadic Balance to Structural Balance

::: {.incremental}
- If a triad is balanced, then it is so **from every member's point of view**.
- We just need to change the interpretation!
- Take this balanced triad and rotate the "you" position around the triangle.
:::

---

## Rotating the "You" Position

```{r}
#| fig.width: 10.2
#| fig.height: 4.6
# Same balanced undirected triad; the focal "you" node rotates
rot_fig <- function(focal, ttl) {
  e <- data.frame(from = c("n1", "n1", "n2"), to = c("n2", "n3", "n3"),
                  sign = c("-", "-", "+"))
  g <- graph_from_data_frame(e, directed = FALSE)
  lay <- circ_lay(c("n1", "n2", "n3"))
  labs <- c("n1" = "O", "n2" = "Q", "n3" = "P")
  others <- setdiff(c("O", "Q"), "P")
  labs[setdiff(c("n1", "n2", "n3"), focal)] <- others
  V(g)$lab <- unname(labs[V(g)$name])
  ggraph(g, layout = lay) +
    edge_layer(2.4) + edge_scales() +
    geom_node_point(aes(fill = lab), size = 22, color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("P" = "#F5B7B1", "O" = "#ecf0f1", "Q" = "#ecf0f1")) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = lab), fontface = "bold", size = 8, color = "#2c3e50") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25), ylim = c(-0.95, 1.3), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                           plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")) +
    ggtitle(ttl)
}
rot_fig("n3", "From the lower-left node: \"a friend of an enemy is an enemy\"") +
  rot_fig("n1", "From the top node: \"an enemy of an enemy is a friend\"") +
  rot_fig("n2", "From the lower-right node: \"an enemy of a friend is an enemy\"")
```

---

## Balance as a Triad-Level Property, Regardless of Perspective

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.2
e <- data.frame(from = c("A", "A", "B"), to = c("B", "C", "C"),
                sign = c("-", "+", "-"))
g <- graph_from_data_frame(e, directed = FALSE)
ggraph(g, layout = circ_lay(c("A", "B", "C"))) +
  edge_layer(2.4) + edge_scales() +
  geom_node_point(size = 20, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.8) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 7, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25), ylim = c(-1.1, 1.3), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- This means we can define balance as a **triad-level property regardless of "perspective."**
- For node A: "friends of enemies are enemies."
- For nodes B and C: "enemies of friends are enemies."
- **The triad is balanced for everyone!**
:::
:::
:::

---

## A Signed Graph with Named Edge Sets

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Here is a signed graph with its edge sets named explicitly:
  - One set of vertices $V = \{A, B, C, D, E, F\}$, so $|V| = 6$.
  - Positive links: $E^+ = \{AC, AE, AF, CF, CE\}$, so $|E^+| = 5$.
  - Negative links: $E^- = \{AB, BC, BD, CD, DF, EF\}$, so $|E^-| = 6$.
- The graph is $G = \{V, E^+, E^-\}$.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.4
#| fig.height: 4.4
sg6_e <- rbind(
  data.frame(from = c("A", "A", "A", "A", "C", "C", "C", "D", "E"),
             to   = c("B", "C", "E", "F", "D", "E", "F", "F", "F"),
             sign = c("-", "+", "+", "+", "-", "+", "+", "-", "-")),
  data.frame(from = c("B", "B"), to = c("C", "D"), sign = c("-", "-"))
)
sg6 <- graph_from_data_frame(sg6_e, directed = FALSE)
ggraph(sg6, layout = circ_lay(LETTERS[1:6])) +
  edge_layer() + edge_scales() +
  geom_node_point(size = 16, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.6) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 6, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::
:::

---

## Building Its Adjacency Matrix, Step 1

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.2
ggraph(sg6, layout = circ_lay(LETTERS[1:6])) +
  edge_layer(1.9) + edge_scales() +
  geom_node_point(size = 14, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.5) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 5, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- The adjacency matrix of a signed graph works just like an ordinary adjacency matrix, except each entry records the **sign** of the tie.
- **Step 1**: draw the empty grid with `--` on the diagonal.
:::

```{r}
sg6_m0 <- matrix("", 6, 6, dimnames = list(LETTERS[1:6], LETTERS[1:6]))
diag(sg6_m0) <- "--"
signed_kbl(sg6_m0, font = 24, color_cells = FALSE)
```
:::
:::

---

## Building Its Adjacency Matrix, Step 2

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.2
ggraph(sg6, layout = circ_lay(LETTERS[1:6])) +
  edge_layer(1.9) + edge_scales() +
  geom_node_point(size = 14, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.5) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 5, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **Step 2**: put a **1** where nodes are linked by a positive line.
:::

```{r}
sg6_m1 <- matrix("", 6, 6, dimnames = list(LETTERS[1:6], LETTERS[1:6]))
diag(sg6_m1) <- "--"
for (pr in list(c("A","C"), c("A","E"), c("A","F"), c("C","F"), c("C","E"))) {
  sg6_m1[pr[1], pr[2]] <- sg6_m1[pr[2], pr[1]] <- "1"
}
signed_kbl(sg6_m1, font = 24, color_cells = TRUE)
```
:::
:::

---

## Building Its Adjacency Matrix, Step 3

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.2
ggraph(sg6, layout = circ_lay(LETTERS[1:6])) +
  edge_layer(1.9) + edge_scales() +
  geom_node_point(size = 14, fill = "#ecf0f1", color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.5) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 5, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **Step 3**: put a **−1** where nodes are linked by a negative line, and a **0** where nodes are not adjacent.
:::

```{r}
sg6_mf <- matrix("0", 6, 6, dimnames = list(LETTERS[1:6], LETTERS[1:6]))
diag(sg6_mf) <- "--"
for (pr in list(c("A","C"), c("A","E"), c("A","F"), c("C","F"), c("C","E"))) {
  sg6_mf[pr[1], pr[2]] <- sg6_mf[pr[2], pr[1]] <- "1"
}
for (pr in list(c("A","B"), c("B","C"), c("B","D"), c("C","D"), c("D","F"), c("E","F"))) {
  sg6_mf[pr[1], pr[2]] <- sg6_mf[pr[2], pr[1]] <- "-1"
}
signed_kbl(sg6_mf, font = 24, color_cells = TRUE)
```
:::
:::

---

## Symmetric Cells Have the Same Value

```{r}
signed_kbl(sg6_mf, font = 24, color_cells = TRUE)
```

::: {.incremental}
- Because the graph is undirected, the matrix is a **symmetric valued matrix**: symmetric cells have the same value!
- For example $a_{1,3} = a_{3,1} = 1$ (the positive A–C link).
- And $a_{2,4} = a_{4,2} = -1$ (the negative B–D link).
:::

---

## Structural Balance Applies to Complete Signed Graphs

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Structural Balance Theory applies to **complete signed graphs**.
- A complete signed graph is a graph in which **every node is connected to every other** by either a positive line or a negative line.
- No zeros anywhere off the diagonal.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.4
#| fig.height: 4.4
# Complete signed graph: factions {A, B, F} and {C, D, E}
comp_e <- rbind(
  comp_pairs(c("A","B","F"), c("A","B","F"), "+"),
  comp_pairs(c("C","D","E"), c("C","D","E"), "+"),
  comp_pairs(c("A","B","F"), c("C","D","E"), "-")
)
comp <- graph_from_data_frame(comp_e, directed = FALSE)
fac_map <- c("A" = "#AED6F1", "B" = "#AED6F1", "F" = "#AED6F1",
             "C" = "#F5B7B1", "D" = "#F5B7B1", "E" = "#F5B7B1")
comp_plot <- function(node_size = 15, lab = 5.5, edge_w = 2.2) {
  ggraph(comp, layout = circ_lay(c("A", "B", "F", "C", "D", "E"))) +
    edge_layer(edge_w) + edge_scales() +
    geom_node_point(size = node_size, aes(fill = name), color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fac_map) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = lab, color = "#2c3e50") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
}
comp_plot() + labs(title = "Complete undirected signed graph") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                         plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"))
```
:::
:::

---

## The Complete Signed Graph as a Matrix

<div class="table-dense" style="font-size: 95%;">

```{r}
ord6 <- c("A", "B", "F", "C", "D", "E")
comp_m <- matrix("-1", 6, 6, dimnames = list(ord6, ord6))
diag(comp_m) <- "--"
for (pr in list(c("A","B"), c("A","F"), c("B","F"), c("C","D"), c("C","E"), c("D","E"))) {
  comp_m[pr[1], pr[2]] <- comp_m[pr[2], pr[1]] <- "1"
}
signed_kbl(comp_m, color_cells = TRUE)
```

</div>

::: {.incremental}
- Every off-diagonal cell is filled: $+1$ within each group, $-1$ between the groups.
- Every one of the $\binom{6}{3} = 20$ triples is a triad we can check.
:::

---

## Balance as a Whole-Network Property

::: {.incremental}
- When a whole signed graph **only contains balanced triads**, then the graph is also **balanced**.
- Balance can be a **whole-network property**!
- A signed graph in which every triple is balanced is called a **balanced signed graph**.
- Checking twenty triads by hand sounds tedious — there is a shortcut.
:::

---

## The Triad-Checking Shortcut

::: {.incremental}
- **Trick**: a triad is **balanced** if it has either **zero or two negative** links.
- A triad is **unbalanced** if the number of negative links is **odd** (one or three).
- This follows directly from sign multiplication: the product of the edge signs is positive exactly when an even number of them is negative.
:::

---

## Checking the Complete Graph, Triad by Triad

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.2
comp_plot(node_size = 14, lab = 5, edge_w = 1.9)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- ABF triad: three positive links. **Balanced!**
- ABC triad: one positive (A–B), two negative. **Balanced!**
- CDF triad: C–D positive, C–F and D–F negative. **Balanced!**
- BEF triad: B–F positive, B–E and E–F negative. **Balanced!**
- ACE triad: A–C and A–E negative, C–E positive. **Balanced!**
- And so on for all the triads. Every one checks out.
:::
:::
:::

---

## The Fundamental Theorem of Structural Balance

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- The fundamental theorem of structural balance was discovered by the mathematicians **Dorwin Cartwright and Frank Harary** in 1956.
- It states that when a graph is balanced, it can be **split into two groups** such that there are:
  - Only **positive links within** groups.
  - Only **negative links between** groups.
- **Balance is not necessarily good!** Structural balance is equivalent to perfect **group polarization**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.2
#| fig.height: 4.2
comp_plot(node_size = 14, lab = 5, edge_w = 1.9)
```
:::
:::

---

## Seeing the Blocks: Reorder the Matrix

<div class="table-dense" style="font-size: 95%;">

```{r}
signed_kbl(comp_m, color_cells = TRUE)
```

</div>

::: {.incremental}
- We can see the two-group structure if we **rearrange the rows and columns** of the signed adjacency matrix.
- Put the friends of A first (A, B, F), then the enemies of A (C, D, E).
:::

---

## The Block-Diagonal Structure

<div class="table-dense" style="font-size: 95%;">

```{r}
signed_kbl(comp_m, color_cells = TRUE)
```

</div>

::: {.incremental}
- In the reordered matrix the positives cluster into two **blocks on the diagonal**.
- The off-diagonal blocks are all negative.
- This is the matrix signature of perfect polarization: two camps, positive inside, hostile across.
:::

---

## Structural Balance in Everyday Life

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **P** (a liberal retweeter), **O** (a liberal tweeter), **Q** (a liberal tweet):
  - All sentiments positive. A balanced triad.
- **P** (a conservative retweeter), **O** (a conservative tweeter), **Q** (a conservative tweet):
  - Also all positive. Another balanced triad.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **P** (a liberal retweeter), **O** (a conservative tweeter), **Q** (a conservative tweet):
  - Negative sentiments all around. An unbalanced triad.
- In a balanced platform, liberal accounts retweet liberal content and conservative accounts retweet conservative content, and each side disparages the other's.
- Balance at the triad level aggregates into **echo chambers** at the network level.
:::
:::
:::

---

## Adding New Nodes Preserves the Polarization Pattern

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="36%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Adding new nodes to the structure does not change the group polarization pattern, **as long as their relationships to every other node are balanced**.
- New nodes **H** and **I** (yellow) join.
- I makes friends with C, D, and E.
- H makes friends with A, B, and F.
- Then they balance out the rest of the relationships with the other side.
- **Still polarized!**
:::
:::

::: {.column width="64%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 6.4
#| fig.height: 3.4
# Add H (joins A, B, F side) and I (joins C, D, E side)
ext_e <- rbind(
  comp_e,
  comp_pairs(c("H"), c("A","B","F"), "+"),
  comp_pairs(c("H"), c("C","D","E","I"), "-"),
  comp_pairs(c("I"), c("C","D","E"), "+"),
  comp_pairs(c("I"), c("A","B","F"), "-"),
  data.frame(from = "H", to = "I", sign = "-")
)
ext <- graph_from_data_frame(ext_e, directed = FALSE)
ord8 <- c("A", "B", "F", "H", "C", "D", "E", "I")
# New nodes H and I in yellow so they stand out
ext_map <- c(fac_map, "H" = "#F9E79F", "I" = "#F9E79F")
# Two camp layout: faction 1 on the left, faction 2 on the right
ext_lay <- rbind(
  c(-0.50,  0.80), c(-0.95,  0.30), c(-0.95, -0.40), c(-0.50, -0.85),
  c( 0.50,  0.80), c( 0.95,  0.30), c( 0.95, -0.40), c( 0.50, -0.85)
)
rownames(ext_lay) <- ord8
colnames(ext_lay) <- c("x", "y")
new_stroke <- function(g) ifelse(V(g)$name %in% c("H", "I"), 2.4, 1.4)
before_panel <- ggraph(comp, layout = circ_lay(c("A", "B", "F", "C", "D", "E"))) +
  edge_layer(1.9) + edge_scales() +
  geom_node_point(size = 12, aes(fill = name), color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = fac_map) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 4.4, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                         plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")) +
  ggtitle("Before: 6 nodes")
after_panel <- ggraph(ext, layout = ext_lay[V(ext)$name, , drop = FALSE]) +
  edge_layer(1.9) + edge_scales() +
  geom_node_point(size = 12, aes(fill = name), color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21,
                  stroke = new_stroke(ext)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ext_map) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 4.4, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                         plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")) +
  ggtitle("After: add H and I (yellow)")
# Original-style single-panel plot used by later slides
ext_plot <- function(node_size = 13, lab = 4.6, edge_w = 2) {
  ggraph(ext, layout = ext_lay[V(ext)$name, , drop = FALSE]) +
    edge_layer(edge_w) + edge_scales() +
    geom_node_point(size = node_size, aes(fill = name), color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = ext_map) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = lab, color = "#2c3e50") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
}
before_panel + after_panel + plot_layout(nrow = 1)
```
:::
:::

---

## Properties of Balanced Signed Graphs

::: {.incremental}
- Balanced signed graphs have some interesting properties. If a graph $G$ is balanced:
  - **Any subgraph of $G$ is also balanced.**
  - **All paths between the same pair of nodes have the same sign** as the link between them.
  - **Cycles of any length are always positive** (an even number of negative edges).
:::

```{r}
#| fig.width: 6.2
#| fig.height: 3.2
# Two balanced subgraphs of the complete signed graph
sub_panel <- function(nodes, ttl) {
  sg <- induced_subgraph(comp, nodes)
  ggraph(sg, layout = circ_lay(nodes)) +
    edge_layer(2) + edge_scales() +
    geom_node_point(size = 15, aes(fill = name), color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fac_map) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 5.5, color = "#2c3e50") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                           plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold")) +
    ggtitle(ttl)
}
sub_panel(c("A", "C", "E"), "Subgraph {A, C, E}: balanced") +
  sub_panel(c("A", "B", "F"), "Subgraph {A, B, F}: balanced")
```

---

## The Sign of a Path

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.4
#| fig.height: 4.4
# Highlight the path F - B - A - C - I
path_pairs <- list(c("F","B"), c("B","A"), c("A","C"), c("C","I"))
name_key <- function(pairs) {
  vapply(pairs, function(p) paste(sort(p), collapse = "|"), "")
}
path_idx <- function(l) {
  ed <- get_edges()(l)
  nm <- V(ext)$name
  key <- paste(pmin(nm[ed$from], nm[ed$to]), pmax(nm[ed$from], nm[ed$to]), sep = "|")
  ed[key %in% name_key(path_pairs), ]
}
# Muted base edges so the highlighted path stands out
ggraph(ext, layout = ext_lay[V(ext)$name, , drop = FALSE]) +
  geom_edge_link(color = "grey72", width = 1.4,
                 end_cap = circle(9, "mm"), start_cap = circle(9, "mm")) +
  geom_edge_link(data = path_idx, color = "#E67E22", width = 3.4,
                 end_cap = circle(9, "mm"), start_cap = circle(9, "mm")) +
  geom_node_point(size = 13, aes(fill = name), color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ext_map) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 4.6, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- The **sign of a path** is the **product of the signs** of each edge in it.
- $F$ and $I$ have a negative connection.
- All paths connecting F and I are **negative**:
  - F–B–A–C–I: $(+1)(+1)(-1)(+1) = -1$
  - F–B–E–I: $(+1)(-1)(+1) = -1$
- Positively connected nodes like E and C have **all positive paths**:
  - E–I–C: $(+1)(+1) = +1$
  - E–D–C: $(+1)(+1) = +1$
:::
:::
:::

---

## Cycles Are Always Positive

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.4
#| fig.height: 4.4
# Highlight two cycles: A-C-B (triangle) and A-C-D-E-B (5-cycle)
cyc_pairs <- list(c("A","C"), c("C","B"), c("B","A"),
                  c("C","D"), c("D","E"), c("E","B"))
cyc_idx <- function(l) {
  ed <- get_edges()(l)
  nm <- V(ext)$name
  key <- paste(pmin(nm[ed$from], nm[ed$to]), pmax(nm[ed$from], nm[ed$to]), sep = "|")
  ed[key %in% name_key(cyc_pairs), ]
}
# Muted base edges so the highlighted cycles stand out
ggraph(ext, layout = ext_lay[V(ext)$name, , drop = FALSE]) +
  geom_edge_link(color = "grey72", width = 1.4,
                 end_cap = circle(9, "mm"), start_cap = circle(9, "mm")) +
  geom_edge_link(data = cyc_idx, color = "#E67E22", width = 3.4,
                 end_cap = circle(9, "mm"), start_cap = circle(9, "mm")) +
  geom_node_point(size = 13, aes(fill = name), color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ext_map) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 4.6, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.incremental}
- In a balanced signed graph, **cycles of any length are always positive**.
- 3-cycle A–C–B: $(-1)(-1)(+1) = +1$
- 5-cycle A–C–D–E–B: $(-1)(+1)(+1)(-1)(+1) = +1$
- Equivalent statement: every cycle contains an **even number of negative edges**.
:::
:::
:::

---

# Part 5: From Balance to Clustering

---

## Clustering Is a Weaker Criterion Than Balance

::: {.incremental}
- Balance demands two groups. But real signed networks often have **more than two** clusters.
- **Davis's insight**: clustering is a **weaker criterion** than balance.
- A signed graph is **clusterable** when we can partition the nodes into clusters such that:
  - Positive links fall **within** clusters.
  - Negative links fall **between** clusters.
- The all-negative triad — unbalanced under strict balance — is now **allowed**.
:::

---

## Building a Clusterable Network, Step 1: Positive Links Within Clusters

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Suppose we build a network whose triangles come in only three types:
  - **All-positive** triads (everybody inside a cluster likes everybody else in it).
  - **Two-negative** triads (two cluster-mates against an outsider).
  - **All-negative** triads (one node from each of three clusters).
- **Step 1**: draw the **positive** links inside each of three clusters: $\{a, d, e\}$, $\{c, g, i\}$, and $\{b, f, h\}$.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 5.2
#| fig.height: 4.8
# 9-node clusterable signed graph: clusters {a,d,e}, {c,g,i}, {b,f,h}
cl_pairs <- function(g1, sign) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(g1)[-1], function(k)
    data.frame(from = g1[k], to = g1[1], sign = sign)))
}
clus_nodes <- c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f", "g", "h", "i")
three_clus <- list(c("a","d","e"), c("c","g","i"), c("b","f","h"))
clus_e <- rbind(
  cl_pairs(three_clus[[1]], "+"),
  cl_pairs(three_clus[[2]], "+"),
  cl_pairs(three_clus[[3]], "+"),
  comp_pairs(three_clus[[1]], three_clus[[2]], "-"),
  comp_pairs(three_clus[[1]], three_clus[[3]], "-"),
  comp_pairs(three_clus[[2]], three_clus[[3]], "-")
)
clus <- graph_from_data_frame(clus_e, directed = FALSE)
cl_map <- c("a" = "#AED6F1", "d" = "#AED6F1", "e" = "#AED6F1",
            "c" = "#ABEBC6", "g" = "#ABEBC6", "i" = "#ABEBC6",
            "b" = "#F5B7B1", "f" = "#F5B7B1", "h" = "#F5B7B1")
# Three-cluster layout: each cluster a tight triangle around its centroid
mk_clus_lay <- function(cx, cy, names, r = 0.38) {
  ang <- pi/2 - (0:(length(names) - 1)) * (2 * pi / length(names))
  m <- cbind(x = cx + r * cos(ang), y = cy + r * sin(ang))
  rownames(m) <- names
  m
}
clus_lay <- rbind(mk_clus_lay(-1.05,  0.90, three_clus[[1]], r = 0.34),
                  mk_clus_lay( 1.05,  0.90, three_clus[[2]], r = 0.34),
                  mk_clus_lay( 0.00, -1.05, three_clus[[3]], r = 0.34))
pos_idx <- function(l) { ed <- get_edges()(l); ed[ed$sign == "+", ] }
clus_plot <- function(node_size = 15, lab = 6, edge_w = 1.7) {
  ggraph(clus, layout = clus_lay[V(clus)$name, , drop = FALSE]) +
    edge_layer(edge_w) + edge_scales() +
    geom_node_point(size = node_size, aes(fill = name), color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.6) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cl_map) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = lab, color = "#2c3e50") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.60, 1.60), ylim = c(-1.55, 1.45), clip = "off") +
    theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
}
# Step 1 view: positive links only
ggraph(clus, layout = clus_lay[V(clus)$name, , drop = FALSE]) +
  geom_edge_link(data = pos_idx, color = pos_col, width = 2.4,
                 end_cap = circle(9, "mm"), start_cap = circle(9, "mm")) +
  geom_node_point(size = 16, aes(fill = name), color = "#2c3e50", shape = 21, stroke = 1.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cl_map) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), fontface = "bold", size = 6, color = "#2c3e50") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.60, 1.60), ylim = c(-1.55, 1.45), clip = "off") +
  theme_slides() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::
:::

---

## Building a Clusterable Network, Step 2: Negative Links Between Clusters

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
::: {.incremental}
- **Step 2**: connect **every** pair of nodes in **different** clusters with a **negative** link.
- Every cluster is now a positive island in a sea of negatives.
- The graph is complete: every pair of nodes is tied, positively or negatively.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 5.2
#| fig.height: 4.8
clus_plot()
```
:::
:::

---

## The Adjacency Matrix of the Clusterable Network

```{r}
clus_m <- matrix("-1", 9, 9, dimnames = list(clus_nodes, clus_nodes))
diag(clus_m) <- "--"
for (pr in list(c("a","d"), c("a","e"), c("d","e"), c("c","g"), c("c","i"), c("g","i"),
                c("b","f"), c("b","h"), c("f","h"))) {
  clus_m[pr[1], pr[2]] <- clus_m[pr[2], pr[1]] <- "1"
}
signed_kbl(clus_m, color_cells = TRUE)
```

::: {.incremental}
- Positives ($+1$, green) sit inside each of the three clusters; negatives ($-1$, red) sit between them.
- Triads entirely within a cluster are all-positive; triads spanning two clusters have two negatives; triads spanning all three are all-negative.
:::

---

## Davis Shows That the Graph Has Three Clusters

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig.width: 4.6
#| fig.height: 4.4
clus_plot(node_size = 14, lab = 5.5, edge_w = 2)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Davis shows that the nodes partition into three clusters:
  - **Cluster 1**: $\{a, d, e\}$
  - **Cluster 2**: $\{c, g, i\}$
  - **Cluster 3**: $\{b, f, h\}$
- Positive links within clusters, negative links between them.
- The all-negative triads (like $\{a, b, c\}$, one node from each cluster) are what keep this from being strictly **balanced** — but it is perfectly **clusterable**.
:::
:::
:::

---

## The Cluster Structure in the Reordered Matrix

```{r}
signed_kbl(clus_m, color_cells = TRUE)
```

::: {.incremental}
- Reordering rows and columns by cluster exposes **three positive blocks on the diagonal**.
- Every off-diagonal block is negative.
- Balance gives two camps; clusterability generalizes the same logic to **any number of clusters**.
:::
